The historical evidence returned was OCR text from [Britannica page 1614](https://huggingface.co/datasets/NationalLibraryOfScotland/encyclopaedia_britannica_illustrated/tree/309f765b1ecc83e0a7f7762e44b4a927a7555443), a **mismatched source** containing entries on thistles, Thomas, and related topics, with only a cross-reference to astronomy rather than an astronomy article.  
Modern evidence included Wikipedia’s [Cultural astronomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1298337464), describing how cultures interpret celestial objects, plus [Astronomy education](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1327518763), [Institute of Astronomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=974317131), and [Astronomy (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1346230266).  
Retrieval was partial because the embedding service returned HTTP 503 errors, leaving lexical matching only, so these results do not support a reliable historical-versus-modern comparison of astronomical knowledge.
